To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ETC representation assignments that adequately suppress the neutral flavor-changing processes also lead to realistic CKMs, and that the ETC representations for quarks and leptons can be assigned independently.

ETC models with $L$ and/or $R$ components assigned to relatively conjugates representations of the ETC gauge group are not consistent with neutral flavor-changing processes, and that ETC models that are consistent with neutral flavor changing processes can also be consistent with other flavor-changing processes.

the ETC representation assignments that are most consistent with the flavor-changing processes that we analyze are those in which the $U$-type quark doublets are assigned to a fundamental representation of the ETV group, while the $D$- and $L$-type doublets are assigned either to a fundamental representation or a conjugate-fundament representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the flavor-changing processes that are induced in ETC models by dimension-six four-fermionic operators.
the question of whether the flavor-changing processes in ETC models can be adequately suppressed by a judicious representation assignment of quarks and leptons.
the question of how to reconcile the existence of the Cabibbo-Kobayashi-Maskawa mixing matrix with the absence of flavor-changing neutral currents in nature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class of models we consider is not ruled out by the available experimental data, but is severely constrained.

ETC models in which the $SU(2)_L$ doublet and singlet components of the quark and lepton fields are assigned to the {\it same} ETC representation, can adequately suppress all flavor-changing processes.
ETC models with $L\ensuremath{-}{R}$ representations of the quarks are viable.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ETC models with the most promising phenomenology are those in which the ETC group commutes with the standard model group.
the ETC model building is not yet over.
the ETC gauge group must be a product of a simple group and a ${Z}_{2}$, and that the left- and the right-handed fermions must be in the same representation of the simple group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, if ETC gauge interactions do not commute with those of the standard model, they can induce flavor-changing neutral currents, and the resulting constraints are severe.
the $L$- and $R$-component assignments for the quarks and leptons must be carefully chosen, and cannot be chosen arbitrarily.
the ETC gauge group should be made to commute with the SM gauge group.
